repositories.name: JetBrains/thinkrail
repositories.description: Vibe code with pi in a lightweight, real IDE that customises itself around the way you work — The Vibe You Need

en.purpose: An agent-focused IDE built around the pi coding agent, combining code editing, isolated workspaces, and durable project knowledge.
highlights: Git worktrees give parallel tasks separate branches and working directories, with integrated pull request and review controls.
A Monaco editor, terminals, file changes, and anchored review comments sit beside the agent conversation.
Living SPEC.md documents and reusable skills preserve project intent across sessions.

en.purpose: A modular collection of design skills for AI coding tools that can read Markdown rules.
highlights: Skills live in self-contained folders, so users install only the ones they need.
The current landing-page-design skill covers intake questions, page structure, and conversion copy.
Its visual guidance includes typography, spacing, corner radius, and motion; support is not tied to one coding agent.

repositories.name: obra/superpowers
repositories.description: An agentic skills framework & software development methodology that works.

en.purpose: A composable skills framework that gives coding agents a software development process, from clarifying requirements to reviewing and finishing changes.
highlights: Turns an agreed design into small implementation tasks with explicit files and verification steps.
Includes test-driven development, systematic debugging, and verification-before-completion skills.
Supports isolated worktrees and either task-by-task agent execution or an inline implementation workflow with review.

en.purpose: An agent-native learning workspace connecting personalized tutoring, problem solving, quizzes, research, and study practice.
highlights: Learning modes share a capability runtime and session context while keeping workflows tailored to each task.
Reuses knowledge bases, books, notebooks, question banks, and memory across supported learning workflows.
Video reading combines playback, transcript search, timestamp-grounded tutoring, saved notes, and resumable progress.

repositories.name: macro-inc/macro
repositories.description: Macro is a unified workspace for teams: email, chat, docs, tasks, agents, calls, and CRM — @-linked together with shared AI memory.

en.purpose: A shared team workspace that brings email, messages, documents, tasks, agents, and CRM into one connected system.
highlights: Cross-references between documents, tasks, messages, and emails form a native bidirectional graph.
Collaborative Markdown documents use CRDTs, alongside purpose-built inboxes, channels, tasks, and canvases.
Team-level agent memory can draw on connected workspace content, including recorded and transcribed calls.

repositories.name: Nutlope/hallmark
repositories.description: Anti-AI-slop design skill for Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex.

en.purpose: A design skill for coding agents that builds and reviews websites around their actual purpose while reducing repetitive AI-generated visual patterns.
highlights: Provides fifty visual themes and a custom design path driven by the user's brief.
Uses a real browser to check the result, with separate accessibility, layout, and design-detail gates.
Offers redesign and audit workflows and can capture the user's actual site or app as visual context.

repositories.name: pbakaus/impeccable
repositories.description: The design vocabulary for your coding agent. Steer with polish and bolder, review with critique and audit, catch AI slop before it ships.

en.purpose: A design vocabulary and review toolkit that helps coding agents improve existing interfaces through targeted visual instructions.
highlights: Commands such as polish, bolder, and critique express specific design changes rather than vague requests.
Audits cover accessibility, performance, theming, and responsive behavior, with findings prioritized by severity.
A deterministic checker flags 62 common design and quality problems without requiring an LLM or API key for that check.

repositories.name: makecindy/cindy
repositories.description: Consider it done. The open-source AI agent that works out of the box · 想到，就能做到。开源、开箱即用的 AI Agent。

en.purpose: An open-source AI agent client that connects computers and phones so users can continue work across devices with their existing agent tools and model providers.
highlights: Continues sessions across connected devices and offers remote access to files, providers, and the desktop when enabled.
Brings Claude Code, Codex, and Pi into one interface, with supported subscriptions, API providers, and local models.
This repository contains desktop and mobile clients plus shared packages; the backend is maintained separately.

repositories.name: nightly-labs/openbot
repositories.description: A local-first desktop workspace for persistent AI teammates. Run Codex, Claude, and Grok with dedicated workspaces, task queues, file sharing, browser control, and agent-to-agent collaboration.

en.purpose: A local-first desktop workspace for persistent AI teammates, each with its own conversation, working directory, and agent provider.
highlights: Supports several coding-agent backends and ACP integrations, with per-agent model and context settings.
Persistent message queues, agent messaging, file transfers, and shared channels coordinate ongoing work.
An embedded browser and optional computer-use tools extend agents beyond terminal commands; the project is a development preview.

en.purpose: A research-oriented collection of model prompts and agent configuration examples for studying instruction handling and model behavior.
highlights: Covers system prompts, persona definitions, workspace policies, and agent operating specifications.
Includes examples for closed and open-weight model families and several agent-specific configuration formats.
The README frames the material as research on instruction conflicts and resistance to prompt injection.

repositories.name: hmjz100/LinkSwift
repositories.description: 一个基于 JavaScript 的网盘文件下载地址获取工具。基于【网盘直链下载助手】修改 ，支持 百度网盘 / 阿里云盘 / 中国移动云盘 / 天翼云盘 / 迅雷云盘 / 夸克网盘 / UC网盘 / 123云盘 八大网盘

en.purpose: A browser userscript that obtains direct download links from supported cloud drives and connects them to external download tools.
highlights: Supports nine cloud-drive services, including Baidu, Aliyun, Quark, and 123pan.
Combines direct-link retrieval, interface customization, and integrations with download managers.
Uses providers' public APIs; the README explicitly distinguishes link retrieval from bypassing download speed limits.

repositories.name: expo/skills
repositories.description: A collection of AI agent skills for working with Expo projects and Expo Application Services

en.purpose: Official Expo skills that teach coding agents how to build, debug, upgrade, and deploy Expo and React Native applications.
highlights: Framework skills cover routing, native UI, animation, data fetching, native modules, and SDK upgrades.
Separately labels workflows involving paid EAS services, including builds, hosting, updates, and observability.
Plugin installations bundle an Expo MCP connection for live documentation and development workflows.

repositories.name: ruvnet/RuView
repositories.description: π RuView turns commodity WiFi signals into real-time spatial intelligence, vital sign monitoring, and presence detection — all without a single pixel of video.

en.purpose: A WiFi sensing project exploring presence detection and spatial awareness without cameras, with integrations for smart-home systems.
highlights: Exposes room and sensor signals through Home Assistant and other supported smart-home integrations.
Documents separate maturity levels for validated checkpoints, experimental on-device models, and architecture-only components.
Benchmark pose results are distinct from live single-ESP32 performance; the README identifies limitations and a still-stubbed on-device pose path.

repositories.name: xiaolai/the-craft-of-selfteaching
repositories.description: One has no future if one couldn't teach themself.

en.purpose: Li Xiaolai's open-source book on self-teaching, distributed as notebooks that readers can study locally and help improve.
highlights: Recommends a local JupyterLab setup for an interactive reading experience.
Links to a separate Markdown edition for readers who prefer plain-text documents.
Provides a pull request proofreading workflow so readers can contribute corrections.
